page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The processing power is delivered by an Intel Xeon CPU running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, supported by 15.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 3.75 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-standard-4 in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-intensive tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1107.78 and a multi-core score of 2904.55, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, Geekbench results show a single-core score of 927.0, which is in the bottom 10%, and a multi-core score of 2044.0, in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 161.64 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 25.29 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 21.61 GB/sec for large-block writes, indicating moderate memory throughput. Cryptographic and compression tasks also show limited throughput, with gzip single-threaded compression reaching 19.01 GB/sec and Passmark CPU encryption scoring 1349.62.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-standard-4 is its legacy hardware profile, which results in lower computational efficiency compared to newer instance families. However, its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio provide predictable performance for baseline workloads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance serves as a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require high-frequency processors or massive memory bandwidth. It is best suited for low-traffic web serving, basic database operations, software compilation tasks, and lightweight background processing.
